question: Which input transformations must preserve the reconstruction (a stable wrong wall is a transformation that deterministically changes it), and which manipulations of run history does the depth cache actually neutralize (a history-dependent wall is one that depends on what ran before, not on declared inputs)?

frozen.base_commit_note: PR #220's head (Witnesses for the clipped coverage grid and fitted ground); Hunter's recon, evaluated as it stood there.
frozen.depth_model: STUBBED, NOT EXERCISED: the MoGe-2 subprocess is replaced by an analytic deterministic renderer (bundles.make_stub_model); no weights, no GPU, no network. recon.depth.rescale is an identity pass (deterministic in depths and poses, holds no history).
frozen.scope_note: This experiment measures repeatability only. No recon repair belongs here: a failing case is recorded as a finding, not fixed. The server branch (t3/server) is not evaluated; recon is absent there.

tolerances.identity_note: identity cases demand byte-identical outputs (deterministic stub, deterministic pipeline)
tolerances.order_note: frames-reordered: the fusion loop sums per-voxel means in list order, so float non-associativity may move the wall; 1.5 mm
tolerances.guarded_note: guarded cases demand the guarded run equal its reference within 0.15 mm of wall

cases.name: baseline-repeat
cases.transformation: none: the same bundle through two fresh work directories
cases.expectation: the floor: both runs ship byte-identical outputs

cases.name: warm-cache
cases.transformation: second run in the same work directory (content-keyed cache hit)
cases.expectation: identical outputs, and the second run calls the model zero times

cases.name: frames-reordered
cases.transformation: scene.json keyframes reversed (frame ids key everything but the fusion loop's order)
cases.expectation: the wall and every output number move by at most order_ft

cases.name: frame-id-duplicate
cases.transformation: a keyframe record repeated (same id, twice)
cases.expectation: the capture refuses it (DuplicateFrameId) before any reconstruction: one depth view must not count from two camera positions

cases.name: image-reencoded
cases.transformation: every keyframe JPEG decoded and re-encoded in place: different bytes, and a lossy re-encode also drifts the decoded pixels slightly
cases.expectation: the key changes (bytes are in it), the cache recomputes, and the JSON outputs are byte-identical with the wall unmoved; the mesh digest may change (vertex colors carry the image bytes), and a real model's invariance to recompression is not claimed

cases.name: intrinsics-shift
cases.transformation: fx/fy +4 px, cx/cy +2 px on every keyframe
cases.expectation: a declared input, so the result may differ; measured, not graded. The key must change (no stale reuse) and no cache folder may be shared

cases.name: unrelated-history
cases.transformation: a second capture (different poses, so a different cache key) runs through the same work directory between two runs of the first
cases.expectation: the first capture's second run is byte-identical to its first: unrelated history cannot touch a content-keyed cache folder

cases.name: stale-cache-pose-edit
cases.transformation: a keyframe's camera moves 0.05 m after a first run, then the same work directory reruns
cases.expectation: the key mismatch sends the rerun to a fresh cache folder; the result equals a fresh run of the edited bundle

cases.name: interrupted-run
cases.transformation: the model process dies after its first depth map (the worker's key file is already written), then the same work directory reruns
cases.expectation: the rerun recomputes the missing maps only and lands on the uninterrupted result

cases.name: same-size-cache-edit
cases.transformation: one cached depth map overwritten with a copy shifted 0.05 m: same shape, same dtype, key.json untouched
cases.expectation: declared guarded: the rerun must equal the baseline within guarded_ft. Whatever the rerun returns when this fails is the history-dependent wall, and a third run records whether the wrong answer is itself stable (run-twice repeatability alone would pass it)
